main.result_summary: The week 2000-W34 consolidation is committed on `main` as `fcfe1f4`, and lint and `sleep-audit.py` were both green on the first full pass. The week had 106 messages: 80 of the 84 with notes are now cited in memory, and the other 4 (m02950, m02983, m02994, m03000) are listed in `dataset/drops/sleep-039.tsv`. A check confirmed every noted message is either cited or dropped. I opened five new topic files: the Azurix UK water valuation, fall 2000 campus recruiting (Berkeley, CMU, MIT), a London analyst's Henwood model question, an option-pricing precision fix in Enron's ERMS risk system, and Mark Lay's distributed-computing question. About 20 existing files got the week's news, including Li Sun joining Research on 28 Aug, Martin Lin's $90K salary plus $10K retention bonus, Gibner's unpaid leave, the London budget and the 18–21 Sep London trip. Six people reached five noted messages and got their own files: Li Sun, Jana Giovannini, Shelly Butler, Michael Anderson, Kristin Gandy and Shmuel Oren. The "John Blumer" alias question passed its 22 Aug due date with no answer, so I closed it as "no alias" with a `(?)` note in `john-bloomer.md`; no new questions were needed. To get past the audit's growth limit and compress, older lines from 25 files moved to `archive/*/2000/*-2000-08-w34.md`, and `speaking-engagements-2000` (the only file above 90% of its size limit) dropped from 2532 to 2340 characters. The five oldest "still true" lines were checked and are still valid. There was no sleep-task, no feedback block and no data source to pull from. One deviation: the run's own notes (the closed question and the new people) are in a separate `memory/archive/inbox/2000-08-26--mail-2.md`, not in `2000-08-26--mail.md` as instructed, because the audit fails when a log is edited while it is being archived, and earlier runs used the same `-2` file. I did not push, as the run instructions said the runner pushes after its own checks. The untracked runner transcript `dataset/runs/sleep-039.
